name: Stokesay Castle

dates.built: c1391-1400 (Historic England listed-building entry 1269939); 1260s-80s and early 1290s (Historic England scheduled-monument entry 1003011)
dates.altered: Gatehouse added C17; entry 1003011 records tree-ring analysis dating the gatehouse timbers to 1639-41.
dates.note: THE TWO HISTORIC ENGLAND ENTRIES FOR THIS SITE DISAGREE ABOUT THE DATE OF THE STANDING FABRIC AND NEITHER IS CHANGED HERE. The listed-building entry 1269939 opens 'Manor house. c1391-1400'; the scheduled-monument entry 1003011 says the castle was 'built in the 1260s-80s and early 1290s by Laurence of Ludlow', ascribes the hall and solar a date circa 1260-80, and puts the south tower after 'a licence to crenellate, granted in 1291'. The node's exemplar year of 1291 is entry 1003011's licence date.

refs.title: Stokesay Castle and Gatehouse Including Moat Retaining Walls, Craven Arms - 1269939 | Historic England
refs.note: Grade I. The Official list entry block prints 'Date first listed: 12-Nov-1954' and 'Date of most recent amendment: 21-Jun-1996'.

refs.title: Stokesay Castle, Craven Arms - 1003011 | Historic England
refs.note: The scheduled-monument entry, read by extract the same day. Its Details section states, as continuous prose: 'Stokesay Castle is one of the finest fortified manor houses in the country, built in the 1260s-80s and early 1290s by Laurence of Ludlow, on the profits of his business as a wool merchant', and describes 'a four-bay, open-hearthed great hall with an extraordinary roof which is a hybrid mixture of raised crucks, aisled end trusses and an unusual example of collar-purlins without crown posts'. Carried here as a ref note and NOT as a survey quote, because a record's survey may name one data_url; nothing in this tree checks prose in a note.

survey.prepared: Date first listed: 12-Nov-1954; Date of most recent amendment: 21-Jun-1996, as the Official list entry block prints them.

quotes.text: Manor house. c1391-1400; gatehouse added C17. Great Hall: sandstone rubble and timber-frame; stone tile roof; spurred brick ridge stack and paired ashlar ridge stack. Gatehouse: timber-frame and plaster on rubble base; stone tile roof with central gable to east; spurred brick ridge stack; stepped rubble exterior stack with C18 brick chimney to south side.
quotes.page: Official list entry, Details, opening paragraph

quotes.text: PLAN: courtyard plan with gatehouse and bridge to east, enclosed by moat with rubble perimeter walls.
quotes.page: Official list entry, Details, PLAN sentence

quotes.text: EXTERIOR: Great Hall: with entrance and 3 mullion and transom 2-light windows under advanced gables; solar cross-wings with hipped roofs; jettied first floor with lattice-glazed mullion windows to north. Tower to south: polygonal; battlemented and embrasured parapet.
quotes.page: Official list entry, Details, EXTERIOR paragraph

quotes.text: 2 storeys and attic; single-window range: 2-light lattice-glazed casement in altered opening, under stop-moulded bressumer; 3-light mullion casement to gable, over moulded bressumer.
quotes.page: Official list entry, Details, EXTERIOR paragraph, the gatehouse sentence; this span is the opening of the extract's second chunk and describes the gatehouse, not the hall range

quotes.text: INTERIOR: in house C17 panelling with carved overmantel; stop-moulded ceiling beams; fireplaces; squints; staircase.
quotes.page: Official list entry, Details, INTERIOR sentence
